Quality vs. speed of Supertonic voices. Fewer steps = faster; more steps = better quality. Applies to the next passages to be prepared. More steps make synthesis slower; on slower phones, high values may cause pauses in guided reading.
Limit for the audio the voices keep so it can be reused. Over the limit, the app deletes the audio used longest ago; anything deleted is simply synthesized again if needed.

Decoding steps per audio frame in Pocket TTS voices. 10 is the default. More steps make synthesis slower and might improve fidelity. Above 10, synthesis gets much slower and may cause pauses in guided reading. Applies to new syntheses; audio already prepared is regenerated when you change this.
Uses more processor cores. It may be faster or slower depending on the phone, and it may heat the device more.
Pause between sentences during guided reading with local voices (Kokoro, Supertonic, Pocket), for more natural cadence.

Pauses that vary like a human narrator\'s: longer at ellipses and at the end of a paragraph, shorter at commas, with a breath after long sentences. Works with every voice. Turn off to use a fixed pause between sentences.

How many text units (paragraph or sentence, depending on the voice engine) guided reading prepares ahead of the one currently playing. Applies to every voice engine. Further ahead: less chance of silence between chunks, but uses more memory/battery and may synthesize text you never end up hearing if you jump to a different spot. Less ahead: saves resources, but raises the risk of pauses if synthesis falls behind reading.

How many syntheses the Kokoro engine can process at the same time (the only voice engine with this option today — the others already process one synthesis at a time). Standard (2) is faster and was tested on a real device. Reduced (1) processes one at a time — slower, but uses less processor at once. Nothing above 2 is offered because it was never tested.
Buffering restored to each voice engine\'s default

How many passages the Supertonic voice prepares at the same time. “One at a time” is how Supertonic has always worked in the app. “Two at a time” is EXPERIMENTAL: it may make reading more fluid, but it was never tested on a real device and the voice may stop mid-book (the app does not close, but reading may fail and need a retry). Test carefully before leaving it on.

This was never tested on a real device. It may cause the Supertonic synthesis process to crash mid-reading (the app itself won\'t crash — you\'d just need to retry that spot). Only enable it if you want to help test this.

Controls the silence inserted between paragraphs during narration.

• 0ms: no pause, continuous reading.
• 300-600ms: natural pause, recommended for most texts.
• 900-1500ms: longer pauses, useful for technical texts or studying.

Longer pauses slightly increase audio generation time.

The app stores synthesized audio chunks in cache.

• Fixed: guided reading and the audiobook no longer both show up in the player. Starting one closes the other and keeps your place.
• The guided reading bar now has an X to close it from any screen.
• Fixed: continuing guided reading from the library started one paragraph before the highlighted one. It now resumes exactly where you stopped.
• Pocket TTS voice: no longer skips the last word of some sentences (like a quoted word at the end), and each sentence starts without a click or echo.
• Supertonic voice: default steps raised from 5 to 8, so it skips fewer words.
• New experimental option in Settings › Natural-sounding voice: “More time for short sentences”, so Supertonic does not swallow words.
• If generating an audiobook fails in the reader, the message now has a “Try again” button.
• Small text fixes.

Read the text below. Ideally 10 to 15 seconds. Recording stops by itself at 30 s; the app uses the best 10-second stretch.

Era uma manhã de **domingo** em **Florianópolis**, e o mar estava **calmo**. _(tom tranquilo)_ Joana abriu a **janela**, respirou fundo e **sorriu**. _(afirmação)_ “Você ouviu o **sino**?” perguntou ela, **curiosa**. _(pergunta, a voz sobe no fim)_ “**Três** passarinhos, **quarenta** e dois barcos e um **grande** arco-íris!” _(animado, com entusiasmo)_ Ela **parou**. _(pausa curta)_ Depois, mais **baixinho**, quase **sussurrando**: _(mais suave)_ “Nem **tudo** o que é **raro** precisa de **razão**.” _(final, voz calma que desce)_ E então o **dia** **começou**.

It was a quiet **Sunday** morning in **Seattle**, and the **ocean** was calm. _(calm tone)_ **Emma** opened the **window**, took a deep **breath**, and **smiled**. _(statement)_ “Did you hear the **bells**?” she asked, **curious**. _(question, voice rises at the end)_ “**Three** little birds, **forty-two** boats, and one **enormous** rainbow!” _(excited, with energy)_ She **paused**. _(short pause)_ Then, **softer**, almost **whispering**: _(gentler)_ “Not everything **rare** needs a **reason**.” _(ending, calm, voice falls)_ And just like that, the **day** **began**.

Era una mañana **tranquila** de **domingo** en **Sevilla**, y el **mar** estaba en **calma**. _(tono tranquilo)_ **Lucía** abrió la **ventana**, respiró **hondo** y **sonrió**. _(afirmación)_ «¿Has oído las **campanas**?» preguntó, **curiosa**. _(pregunta, la voz sube al final)_ «¡**Tres** pajaritos, **cuarenta** y dos barcos y un **enorme** arcoíris!» _(animada, con entusiasmo)_ Se **detuvo**. _(pausa corta)_ Luego, más **bajito**, casi **susurrando**: _(más suave)_ «No todo lo **raro** necesita una **razón**.» _(final, voz calmada que baja)_ Y así, el **día** **empezó**.

Balances quality and speed of Supertonic voice synthesis. Fewer steps = faster; more steps = better quality. Default: 18. Applies to guided reading and audiobook creation. More steps make synthesis slower; on slower phones, high values may cause pauses in guided reading.

To clone a voice, the app needs a free file from Kyutai, the company that created Pocket TTS. You will do 4 simple steps, only once:

1. Sign in to the Hugging Face website with a free account
2. Accept Kyutai's terms of use
3. Download the file (about 220 MB, Wi-Fi is best)
4. Bring the file into the app

You sign in only in your browser. The app never sees or stores your password.

You need a free account on the Hugging Face website. If you already have one, tap I have an account. If not, tap Create free account: the website opens in your browser. After creating it and confirming your email, come back here.

Tap Open page. In your browser, sign in, read the terms and tap the button that agrees and gives you access. The terms forbid cloning another person\'s voice without their clear permission. Then come back here.

Choose the language of the voice you will clone and tap Download. Your browser will save a file called model.safetensors (about 220 MB). Wait for the download to finish and come back here. If the website asks you to accept the terms, go back to step 2.
Tap Choose file and, in the Downloads folder, pick the model.safetensors file you just downloaded.
